evidence.curator_note: Substrate as drawn: the 2-ethylhexanal molecular ion, labelled 'm/z 128' under the structure. The skeleton is printed as C2H5-CH(H)-CH2-CH(C2H5)-CHO with the gamma hydrogen on C4 drawn EXPLICITLY, an aldehyde H on C1, and '+.' printed above the carbonyl oxygen. LOCALIZATION (convention B): the charge and odd electron are written on the oxygen exactly where the page prints them, [CH:1]=[O+:7], not carried only in the JSON fields. Bottom channel: the arrow labelled with a Greek sigma running down-right to the FORMULA 'C4H9+ / m/z 57'. Book draws 0 arc(s) and no product structure, so both moves are curator-supplied. WHICH BUTYL -- this is forced, not chosen: the only four-carbon alkyl in 2-ethylhexanal is C3-C4-C5-C6 (the ethyl branch plus C2 is three carbons), so the cleaved bond must be C2-C3 and the neutral partner is the C4H7O. radical .CH(C2H5)CH=O (71.0497). ENCODING: as in the 'i' channel the oxygen must finish neutral and spin-paired, so the two electrons of the breaking C2-C3 bond are routed one to the oxygen (pairing with its odd electron, move <1>) and one to C2 (the neutral radical's unpaired electron, move <2>), leaving C3 as the butyl cation. CAVEAT, disclosed: the book's sigma label properly denotes ionisation OF the sigma bond, i.e. a charge that was never localised on oxygen at all; this record instead starts from the O-localised molecular ion the page actually DRAWS, which is the same convention IMS9-EQ9.2 adopted for the sigma channel of an alkane. NOTE: 'm/z 57' here is C4H9+ (57.0699), a DIFFERENT ion from the C3H5O+ (57.0335) that the page also labels m/z 57 in the two rearrangement branches -- see IMS9-EQ9.25b and IMS9-EQ9.25c.
